item.title: Non-K\"ahler Hyperbolicity: Surfaces and Codimension One
item.description: arXiv:2611.07098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study hyperbolicity notions for compact complex manifolds defined by special Hermitian metrics and by holomorphic maps from $\mathbb C^{n-1}$ (divisorial hyperbolicity). For surfaces we show that divisorial and Brody hyperbolicity coincide and that Hermitian-symplectic and K\"ahler hyperbolicity coincide when $h^{2,0}=0$. In any dimension we prove obstructions to Gauduchon hyperbolicity, show that projective spaces are not divisorially hyperbolic, and give divisorially hyperbolic manifolds that are not balanced hyperbolic.
item.dc:creator: Samir Marouani

item.title: Sobolev homeomorphisms and Jordan curves with positive area
item.description: arXiv:2611.07322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Each homeomorphic parametrization of a Jordan curve via the unit circle $\mathbb{S}\subset \mathbb{S}^2$ extends to a homeomorphism of the entire $\mathbb{S}^2.$ We show that there exists a Jordan curve of positive area whose every parametrization via $\mathbb{S}$ admits a homeomorphic extension that has $p$-Sobolev regularity on $\mathbb{S}^2$ for all exponents $1\le p<2 .$ This is obtained via a new sharp extension result for the case of $p<2.$
item.dc:creator: Pekka Koskela, Haiqing Xu

item.title: Disproof of a conjecture of Ruscheweyh et al. on universal convexity of Ramanujan generating function
item.description: arXiv:2611.07479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We disprove a conjecture of Ruscheweyh, Salinas and Sugawa concerning the universal convexity of the normalized generating function associated with the Ramanujan sequence $\theta(n).$ More precisely, we prove that the function \[ \sigma(z)=\frac{1}{\theta(1)-1/3}\sum_{n\geq1}(\theta(n)-1/3)z^{n} \] is not universally convex on the slit domain $\mathbb{C}\backslash[1,\infty).$ The proof uses Watson\textquoteright s integral representation of $\theta(n),$ asymptotic estimates for an auxiliary function $h,$ and the representation of derivatives of universally convex functions via logarithmic integrals. As a general extension of this result, we also show that the generalized Ramanujan generating function \[ \sigma_{\alpha}(z)=\frac{1}{\theta(1)-1/3}\sum_{n\geq1}(\theta(n)-1/3)\frac{z^{n}}{n^{\alpha}} \] is universally convex if and only if $\alpha\geq1.$
item.dc:creator: Bing He

item.title: Bergman Kernel Zeros on Rational Hartogs Triangles
item.description: arXiv:2611.07480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Edholm--Mathew nonvanishing conjecture for the palindromic polynomials associated with rational Hartogs triangles. For relatively prime positive integers $m>n$, we show that $e^{-i(m-n)\theta}Q_{m,n}(e^{i\theta})$ is strictly positive for every real $\theta$ and derive an explicit lower bound. The proof expresses this trigonometric polynomial as a finite average of products of unnormalized Fej\'er kernels. It follows that $Q_{m,n}$ has exactly $m-n$ zeros in the punctured unit disc, counted with multiplicity. As a consequence, a rational Hartogs triangle has a zero-free Bergman kernel if and only if its exponent is the reciprocal of a positive integer.
item.dc:creator: Guantie Deng, Qian Fu

item.title: Random complex cross ratios
item.description: arXiv:2611.07670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the cross ratio of four independent points chosen uniformly on the Riemann sphere. A positive integral over a two-dimensional simplex gives its normalized planar density. We then evaluate this integral in terms of the Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm, providing a closed formula. We describe its symmetries, real-axis values, moment bounds and geometric interpretations. We use these to evaluate the mean ideal-tetrahedron volume directly from the density, recovering $\pi/6$, a recent theorem of Kabluchko and Schange. We then prove that the expected distance between two independently sampled hyperbolic geodesics in $\mathbb{H}^3$ is $4/3$, by evaluating the logarithmic potential of the cross-ratio distribution on the negative real axis. Further applications give the joint dihedral-angle density and an exact acute-tetrahedron probability, and a branched-cover probability law on the modular surface with exponentially small cusp tails.
item.dc:creator: Tim Marshall, Gaven Martin

item.title: On Amoebas and the Arithmetic Rigidity of the Mahler Measure
item.description: arXiv:2611.07181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a geometric rigidity theory for Mahler measure based on the global structure of Ronkin functions and amoebas. Our starting point is the theorem of Ronkin describing the affine linearity of the Ronkin function on the complement of the amoeba and the identification of its gradients with lattice points of the Newton polytope. Combining this deep analytic input with convex duality and toric geometry, we show that the vanishing of the Mahler measure is an extremal phenomenon: it occurs if and only if the Ronkin function collapses to the piecewise linear support function of the Newton polytope. This collapse forces a degeneration of the amoeba onto the $(n\!-\!1)$-skeleton of a toric fan and implies that the zero locus of the polynomial is contained in a translate of a codimension-one subtorus. As a first application of this rigidity principle, we recover the generalized Kronecker theorem characterizing Laurent polynomials of vanishing Mahler measure. Our approach bypasses the classical Boyd--Lawton limit formulas and replaces analytic projection arguments by a global convex-geometric and potential-theoretic mechanism rooted in the geometry of amoebas.
item.dc:creator: Mounir Hajli

item.title: On strongly convex K\"ahler--Berwald manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.07752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every real Berwald strongly convex complex Finsler manifold $(M,F,J,\hat\nabla)$, if the Cartan nonlinear connection satisfies the parallelism condition $\hat\nabla J=0$, we construct a good complex vertical connection $D$, prove that $D$ is the complex Rund connection, and $F$ is K\"ahler-Berwald. The inverse direction also can be seen from the construction and proof. As an application, we prove that on an irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $M=G/H$, $G$-invariant complex Finsler metrics are K\"ahler--Berwald. Besides, we obtain the characterization of strongly pseudoconvex holomorphically invariant complex Finsler metrics on the classical domains of type-IV.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoshu Ge

item.title: Space of Geometric Gibbs Measures: Uniqueness, Ergodicity, and Teichm\"uller Complex Manifold Structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.08384v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Building on our previous work, in which geometric Gibbs measures were introduced to complete the space of classical Gibbs measures under the Teichm\"uller metric, we establish the uniqueness of geometric Gibbs measures in this paper. This result completes the construction of a Teichm\"uller complex manifold structure on the space of all geometric Gibbs measures. Using the welding technique, we uncover a connection between geometric Gibbs measures and harmonic measures on dynamical quasicircles. This connection allows us to establish asymptotic conformal rigidity for these dynamical quasicircles. Finally, we establish a foundation for the systematic study of the ergodic properties of geometric Gibbs measures.
item.dc:creator: Yunping Jiang

item.title: Log canonical singularities of plurisubharmonic functions
item.description: arXiv:2312.16140v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A plurisubharmonic weight is \emph{log canonical} if it is at the critical point of turning non-integrable. Given a log canonical plurisubharmonic weight, we show that locally there always exists a log canonical `holomorphic' weight having the same non-integrable locus. The proof uses the theory of quasimonomial valuations developed by Jonsson-Musta\c{t}\u{a} and Xu, as well as the minimal model program over complex analytic spaces due to Fujino and Lyu-Murayama. As a consequence, we obtain that the non-integrable locus is seminormal.
item.dc:creator: Dano Kim, J\'anos Koll\'ar

item.title: On quaternionic analysis and a certain generalized fractal-fractional $\psi$-Fueter operator
item.description: arXiv:2502.15518v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper introduces a fractal $\psi$-Fueter operator in the quaternionic context inspired by the concepts of proportional derivative and Hausdorff derivative ({fractal derivative}) of a function with respect to a fractal measure. Moreover, we establish the corresponding Stokes and Borel-Pompeiu formulas associated to this generalized fractal $\psi$-Fueter operator with respect to a vector valued function induced by truncated exponential functions.
item.dc:creator: Juan Adri\'an Ram\'irez-Belman, Jos\'e Oscar Gonz\'alez-Cervantes, Juan Bory-Reyes

item.title: Kobayashi visibility of strictly convex domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.12502v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that any bounded strictly convex domain in $\Bbb C^N$, endowed with the Kobayashi distance, is visible.
item.dc:creator: Nikolai Nikolov, Amar Deep Sarkar

item.title: A computer-assisted proof of Krzy\.z's conjecture for the sixth coefficient
item.description: arXiv:2610.15206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a computer-assisted approach to Krzy\.z's conjecture based on validated elimination of the masses in an extremal Herglotz representation. The entropy theorem of Lei and Zhang, together with the Agler--McCarthy reduction, leaves only extremals with fewer than $n$ atoms to exclude. In the critical stratum with $n-1$ atoms, the first-order conditions are linear in the masses. Validated local inversion reduces the regular search to $n$ outer parameters, with a rank-free fallback at singular configurations. This gives a proof of the sixth-coefficient conjecture, including its equality statement; the critical-stratum computation takes 8.2 minutes on an M4 Pro. We also obtain an independent proof for the seventh coefficient, recently established by Xie. The computational exclusions use explicit rounding-error bounds, and the equality cases follow analytically.
item.dc:creator: Frank Wikstr\"om

item.title: Bounds for the univalent Bloch-Landau constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.34580v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The univalent Bloch-Landau constant $\mathcal{U}$ is the largest number such that, for every univalent function $f$ on the unit disk, $f(\mathbb{D})$ contains a disk of radius $\mathcal{U}|f'(0)|$. We prove $0.619\le\mathcal{U}<0.6562681$. The previous lower bound, $0.57088586$, came from growth estimates, which control disks centered at $f(0)$, and we show that for Landau-normalized functions such disks cannot give a bound above $0.6$. The main new idea is to move the center of the disk. After Landau's normalization, a compression of the Grunsky matrix constrains every omitted value through the same few coefficients, so a center chosen from these coefficients can be kept away from all omitted values at once. A short analytic proof based on this idea gives $\mathcal{U}\ge0.592$, and a three-row compression, together with pointwise consequences of Landau's normalization, improves the lower bound to $\mathcal{U}\ge0.619$ through an interval certificate. For the upper bound, we construct an explicit domain, bounded by Goodman's first two slit generations, thirty analytic arcs and a circle. We certify $\mathcal{U}<0.6562681$ with a capacity estimate for almost critical arcs, improving the best published bound $0.6563937$.
item.dc:creator: Frank Wikstr\"om

item.title: A convolution inequality and the Krzy\.z conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.05363v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using a sharp bound for convolutions of non-negative trigonometric polynomials with the Fej\'er kernel resembling a pointwise variant of Bernstein's inequality for polynomials, we prove new properties of extremal functions for the Krzy\.z conjecture. In particular, we resolve a 1993 conjecture of Peretz by showing that if $f$ is extremal for some coefficient, then $|f(0)|\leq 1/e$. Furthermore, we show that if equality holds in this estimate for every extremal function, then the Krzy\.z conjecture is true.
item.dc:creator: Sullivan Francis MacDonald

item.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits
item.description: arXiv:2409.18045v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for universality limits for orthogonal polynomials associated to a fixed measure on the real line and related systems. One of our results is that the Christoffel--Darboux kernel has sine kernel asymptotics at a point $\xi$, with regularly varying scaling, if and only if the orthogonality measure (spectral measure) has a unique tangent measure at $\xi$ and that tangent measure is the Lebesgue measure. All previously known cases of sine kernel asymptotics, with absolutely continuous or singular measures, have regularly varying scaling. Our work is not limited to bulk universality; we show that the Christoffel--Darboux kernel has a regularly varying scaling limit with a nontrivial limit kernel if and only if the orthogonality measure has a unique tangent measure at $\xi$ and that tangent measure is not a point mass. The possible limit kernels correspond to homogeneous de Branges spaces; in particular, this equivalence completely characterizes several prominent universality classes such as hard edge universality, Fisher--Hartwig singularities, and jump discontinuities in the weights. A key ingredient in the proof is a new correspondence between measures and chains of de Branges spaces, not between Weyl functions and Hamiltonians. In order to handle limits with power law weights, this correspondence goes beyond the more common setting of Poisson-finite measures, and allows arbitrary power bounded measures.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Eichinger, Milivoje Luki\'c, Harald Woracek

item.title: Algebraic Zhou valuations
item.description: arXiv:2505.19451v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we generalize Zhou valuations, originally defined on complex domains, to the framework of general schemes. We demonstrate that an algebraic version of the Jonsson--Musta\c{t}\u{a} conjecture is equivalent to the statement that every Zhou valuation is quasi-monomial. By introducing a mixed version of jumping numbers and Tian functions associated with valuations, we obtain characterizations of a valuation being a Zhou valuation or computing some jumping number using the Tian functions. Furthermore, we establish the correspondence between Zhou valuations in algebraic settings and their counterparts in analytic settings.
item.dc:creator: Shijie Bao, Qi'an Guan, Lin Zhou

item.title: Kobayashi hyperbolicity of complete linear systems on abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2512.10082v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a geometric condition ensuring that a very general element of a complete linear system on an abelian variety is Kobayashi hyperbolic. This can be seen as the counterpart of some classical results on very general hypersurfaces in projective spaces. Some related conjectures are also given, and involve a natural constant, the so-called basepoint-freeness threshold, associated with any polarized abelian variety $(A, L)$ detecting information about the hyperbolicity of $|L|$.
item.dc:creator: Federico Caucci

item.title: On the First Caustic of Elliptical Billiards
item.description: arXiv:2606.04132v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A point source of light is placed inside a billiard with a smooth, convex, closed boundary. For any integer $n$, the $n$-th caustic by reflection, denoted by $\Gamma_n$, is the envelope of light rays that have undergone $n$ reflections in such a billiard after emanating from the source. It has been conjectured by Gil Bor and Serge Tabachnikov that for an elliptical billiard, $\Gamma_n$ has exactly four ordinary cusps; this problem is a billiard variation of Jacobi's Last Geometric Statement, which concerns the number of cusps in the conjugate locus of a point on an ellipsoid. Gil Bor, Mark Spivakovsky, and Serge Tabachnikov have proven that $\Gamma_n$ has at least four ordinary cusps. In this paper, we present a proof that $\Gamma_1$ has exactly four ordinary cusps, using billiards in complex spaces.
item.dc:creator: Aleksandra Uskova

item.title: A Hardy space approximation supporting zero-free half-planes for the $\zeta$-function
item.description: arXiv:2606.16097v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An equivalent version of the B\'aez-Duarte criterion \cite{baez} for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) by Bagchi states that the RH holds true if and only if the function $E(s) = 1/s$ belongs to the closed linear span of $G_k(s) = (k^{-s} - k^{-1})\zeta(s)/s,\, k \geq 2$ in the Hardy space \( H^2(\mathbb{C}_{1/2}) \), where $\mathbb{C}_{\alpha}$ denotes the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>\alpha$. We first show that if $E$ belongs to the closure of span$(G_k)_{k\geq 2}$ in \( H^2(\mathbb{C}_{\alpha}) \) for $\alpha>1/2$, then $\zeta$ is zero-free in $\mathbb{C}_\alpha$. We then use this as the basis for a numerical analysis of the sequence \[ s_n = \left\| \sum_{k=2}^{n} \mu(k) G_k - E \right\|^2_\alpha, \] for $1/2\leq \alpha \leq 1$, where $\left\|.\right\|_\alpha$ is the norm in $H^2(\mathbb{C}_{\alpha})$ and $\mu$ the M\"obius function.
item.dc:creator: Juan Manzur, Waleed Noor, Gustavo Quintero

item.title: Foliated and Mather-Jacobian discrepancies via tangential arcs
item.description: arXiv:2607.01809v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We express the log discrepancies of co-rank one foliations on normal varieties in terms of arc codimensions and differential orders. On smooth threefolds, if a foliation has simple singularities and its separatrices form an algebraic simple normal crossings divisor, we identify its foliated discrepancies with those of an ordinary pair for every divisor centred on the separatrices. This gives adjunction and log canonical threshold formulae. For algebraic images of the separatrices, we estimate changes in boundary orders caused by failure of ideal generation and by descent through the conductor. For locally complete intersection images, comparison on a common resolution yields criteria for equality of discrepancies and bounds on log canonical thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Maur\'icio Corr\^ea
